briefing.headline: Your biggest gain this week costs nothing: Guéhi (5.76 xP) is sitting on your bench behind Konsa (3.27), and fixing the XI is worth about 3.9 points before you touch a transfer.

do.action: Start Guéhi, Thiaw and Calvert-Lewin; bench Konsa, De Cuyper and Gomez (4-4-3: Raya; Guéhi, Thiaw, Calafiori; B.Fernandes, Mbeumo, Palmer, Tavernier; João Pedro, Calvert-Lewin, Thiago).
do.why: Guéhi 5.76 xP vs Konsa 3.27 is +2.49 on its own; Thiaw 4.56 vs De Cuyper 3.82 is +0.74; Calvert-Lewin 4.71 vs Gomez 4.08 is +0.63. Roughly +3.9 xP for no transfer and no hit. All three are in the predicted XI with 97-100% play probability.

do.action: Move the captaincy off Palmer and onto B.Fernandes.
do.why: Fernandes is your highest projection at 6.12 xP next (30.5 over five) against Palmer's 5.13. Mbeumo at 5.57 is the only other within range. Fernandes has played 90/90 in every game, is first on United's penalties and faces FUL(A) at FDR 3.

do.action: Use one free transfer on Konsa → N.Williams (NFO, £5.0m) and bank the other.
do.why: Williams projects 20.8 over the next five against Konsa's 15.3, a clean +5.5, and 4.95 vs 3.27 next week with COV(H) at FDR 2 then CRY(A). It costs exactly your £0.5m bank, and it frees an Arsenal slot (you currently carry Raya, Calafiori and Konsa, the maximum three). You still hold 2 FTs next week under the accrual rule.

consider.action: Instead of the Williams move, spend both FTs restructuring to Haaland: B.Fernandes + Thiago out, Haaland + a sub-£5.0m midfielder in.
consider.why: For: 99% of the top 10k own Haaland and 97.3% captain him, so every week without him you are betting against the field's captain; he projects 7.72 next and 34.0 over five, the highest in the game. Against: the raw swap is close to neutral — you give up 30.5 (Fernandes) + 23.7 (Thiago) = 54.2 and get back 34.0 plus roughly 18-19 from a cheap midfielder, with the captaincy edge over Fernandes worth about 0.7 a week, so perhaps +2 over five gameweeks. It is also budget-fragile: Fernandes and Thiago raise £19.9m plus £0.5m bank = £20.4m, and no midfielder at £4.9m or below appears in your top-60 list, so you must check the app for an enabler and the site assumes selling at current price. You cannot do this and the Williams move in the same week.

consider.action: Hold De Cuyper in the XI over Thiaw if you want to track the top 10k.
consider.why: For: 45.7% of the top 10k own De Cuyper against 0.7% for Thiaw, so benching him is a live rank risk if Brighton keep a clean sheet at home. Against: the model has De Cuyper at 3.82 vs Thiaw's 4.56 with ARS(H) at FDR 4 versus HUL(H) at FDR 2 — a 0.74 gap is small but it points the other way. At rank 2.96m you are not defending anything, so take the points.

ignore.action: Buying Cherki because half the top 10k have him.
ignore.why: 49.3% top-10k ownership, but 55/90 minutes and 17.3 over five gameweeks — the weakest five-game projection of any premium midfielder in your list. Ownership is a rank risk, not a points case, and this one does not clear the points bar.

ignore.action: Selling Tavernier or Gomez for being obscure.
ignore.why: Tavernier is owned by 2.0% of the top 10k and Gomez 8.7%, but Tavernier's 26.0 over five is the second-best midfield number you own and Gomez's 19.5 is fine for £5.0m. Low ownership at 2.96m overall rank is where you make ground, not where you lose it.

ignore.action: Taking a hit to add Saka or Gibbs-White.
ignore.why: Saka 28.6 and Gibbs-White 25.6 over five against Mbeumo's 27.4 — a gain of at most 1.2, nowhere near the 4 points a hit costs, and neither is affordable from £0.5m anyway.

ignore.action: Dropping Palmer because only 7.3% of the top 10k own him.
ignore.why: 25.0 over five, 87/90 minutes, first on Chelsea's penalties and BRE(A), BOU(H), EVE(A) to come. He is a differential you want, not a problem.

captain.why: 6.12 xP against Mbeumo's 5.57 and Palmer's 5.13. Be clear what this is: 97.3% of the top 10k captain Haaland and only 0.3% captain Fernandes, so a Haaland double-digit haul costs you roughly twenty points against that field. You do not own him, so there is no captain that avoids that; take the highest projection in your own squad rather than hedging.

briefing.chips: No chip this week. You have Free Hit and Bench Boost left from the first set, which expires at the GW19 deadline, but there is no blank or double in the next five gameweeks and no cluster of injuries in your 15 — every player is at 94% play or better. Your optimised bench (Kelleher 3.43, Gomez 4.08, De Cuyper 3.82, Konsa 3.27, about 14.6 points) is healthy enough that Bench Boost will keep; save it for a double gameweek and keep an eye on the GW19 cutoff from around GW14.
risks: Rotowire has published only 10 matches, so 'in predicted XI' is weaker evidence for the rest; check confirmed lineups an hour before the deadline, particularly for Guéhi and Thiaw whom you are promoting into the XI.
Guéhi's 5.76 is inflated by SUN(H) at FDR 2 and a high DefCon probability; his 24.8 over five is still strong, but a single-week spike can miss.

Selling prices are assumed to be current prices. You wildcarded in GW4 so purchase prices are recent and drift should be small, but the Konsa → Williams move uses your bank to the last £0.1m — verify in the app.
If you take the Haaland route instead, you are relying on finding a playable sub-£5.0m midfielder; none appears in your data, and Fernandes at 30.5 over five is the single best projection you own.
Benching De Cuyper (45.7% of the top 10k) on a 0.74 xP margin will look bad if Brighton shut Arsenal out at home.
